title: Blend software Surface horizon with the installed terrain fog color

scope.subject: Reduce the software Surface fallback's hard black-sky/terrain horizon seam by reusing the existing Three.js Scene background color and the installed ProceduralTerrains fog-color contract, without adding textures, alpha compositing, sky/cloud/water layers, new geometry, post-processing or another renderer

research_summary: After SURFACE-SOFTWARE-DEPTH-CUES-001 landed a cheap software arrival beacon, mobile/tablet screenshots still show the main residual composition defect: ProceduralTerrains ends against SurfaceScene's very dark #030b12 background as a visibly hard horizon. The installed procedural-terrains@2.0.5 shader owns its own fog and defaults uFogColor to 0x0b0e14, while Three.js Scene already supports a uniform Color background and its own fog guidance explicitly recommends matching background and fog colors when the goal is a seamless distance fade. Because the custom terrain shader does not rely on host-scene fog, the narrowest candidate is background-color alignment only: software Surface uses #0b0e14, while real-GPU fallback and all other phases keep their existing backgrounds. This adds no draw call, texture, geometry, animation or renderer ownership.

sources.finding: Three.js Scene.background natively accepts a Color, so a uniform horizon/background adjustment requires no new mesh, texture, pass or renderer.
Three.js fog guidance recommends keeping fog and background colors aligned when the intended result is a visually continuous distance fade.
Three.js supports heavier texture/skybox background approaches, but a solid scene background is the lower-cost native option when no sky asset is required.
The installed ProceduralTerrains 2.0.5 remains the fallback terrain subsystem; local inspection of that pinned installed runtime shows its terrain shader default uFogColor is 0x0b0e14.
The existing mobile/tablet Playwright Surface screenshots can judge whether a background-only change materially improves the horizon without introducing a second visual test stack.

search_ladder.conclusion: A replacement sky or environment product is disproportionate for a single hard horizon seam; the existing scene already has a native background authority.
Reuse the current R3F/Three scene background and current Playwright visual acceptance; no new rendering or screenshot framework is needed.
Use the installed terrain runtime's own fog-color contract as the color reference instead of inventing a second atmospheric palette.
Do not add a background image, cubemap, sky dome or other asset for the first probe; a single native scene color has lower cost and directly targets the seam.

candidates.name: Three.js Scene background matched to ProceduralTerrains fog color
candidates.source: Existing R3F <color attach="background"> plus installed ProceduralTerrains uFogColor
candidates.reason: Directly targets the black-sky/terrain seam with zero extra geometry, texture, pass or per-frame work and stays inside the current scene authority.

candidates.name: Existing mobile/tablet Surface Playwright acceptance
candidates.reason: Provides direct before/after evidence on the software-rendered viewports with no new testing infrastructure.

candidates.name: Three.js background texture / skybox
candidates.source: Three.js texture, cubemap or equirectangular Scene.background
candidates.license: MIT engine plus new asset provenance
candidates.reason: Adds texture memory, loading and asset-provenance work before a zero-cost native color probe has been exhausted.

candidates.name: Transparent WebGL canvas with CSS background
candidates.source: Three.js alpha renderer plus CSS background
candidates.reason: Would change Canvas/WebGL alpha ownership across the product and is much broader than a Surface-only horizon seam.

candidates.name: Sky/cloud/water subsystem on software Surface
candidates.source: ProceduralTerrains optional clouds/water or another sky subsystem
candidates.reason: Adds runtime effects on the exact software tier whose cost is tightly bounded; it is not justified before a background-only probe.

decision.rationale: Probe one software-only background color change: match SurfaceScene's existing Three.js background to the installed ProceduralTerrains terrain fog color (#0b0e14), leaving GPU fallback and every other phase unchanged. Promote only if mobile/tablet screenshots materially soften the horizon without reducing foreground/UI readability; otherwise revert and record the negative result rather than escalating inside this task.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: A texture/skybox is broader and more expensive than the native color authority for the specific seam being tested.
Renderer-alpha ownership would cut across the whole shared Canvas for a Surface-only visual defect.
Effect subsystems add continuous software-renderer cost and ownership while a zero-draw background alignment remains available.

decision.fallback: If exact fog-color matching is visually neutral or worse, keep the existing background and close this unit as a negative probe. Any gradient or atmospheric layer requires a new reuse-first task rather than broadening this approval.
